create_coupon.description: Create a discount coupon: a percentage off, a fixed amount off the cart, or a fixed amount off each product. Set an expiry date, a spend range, usage limits, free shipping, and which products, categories or email addresses it applies to.

mock_response.description: 10% off everything for the autumn sale.

create_coupon.name: create_coupon

parameters.description: What shoppers type at checkout. WooCommerce stores it in lower case and refuses a code the store already has.
parameters.name: code

parameters.description: How the discount is worked out. A fixed cart discount when left blank.
parameters.name: discount_type

parameters.description: How much the discount is worth, as a plain number. For a percentage discount this is the percentage: 10 means 10% off, not 0.1.
parameters.name: amount

parameters.description: A note about the coupon, seen only in wp-admin.
parameters.name: description

parameters.description: The last day the coupon works, in the store's own time zone. Never expires when left blank.
parameters.name: expires_on

parameters.description: Stop this coupon being combined with any other.
parameters.name: individual_use

parameters.description: Let this coupon unlock free shipping. Only has an effect if a free-shipping method is set up to require a coupon.
parameters.name: free_shipping

parameters.description: Stop the coupon applying to products already on sale.
parameters.name: exclude_sale_items

parameters.description: The smallest cart total the coupon applies to.
parameters.name: minimum_amount

parameters.description: The largest cart total the coupon applies to.
parameters.name: maximum_amount

parameters.description: How many times the coupon can be used in total.
parameters.name: usage_limit

parameters.description: How many times one customer can use the coupon.
parameters.name: usage_limit_per_user

parameters.description: For a fixed product discount, the most items in the cart it can be applied to.
parameters.name: limit_usage_to_x_items

parameters.description: Product IDs the coupon applies to.
parameters.name: product_ids

parameters.description: Product IDs the coupon must not apply to.
parameters.name: excluded_product_ids

parameters.description: Categories the coupon applies to.
parameters.name: product_category_ids

parameters.description: Categories the coupon must not apply to.
parameters.name: excluded_product_category_ids

parameters.description: Email addresses allowed to use the coupon. Anyone may use it when left blank.
parameters.name: email_restrictions

create_customer.description: Register a customer account on the store, with an email address and optionally a name, username, password and saved addresses. create_order_note.description: Attach a note to an order. A private note is only ever seen in wp-admin; turning on 'Send to customer' makes WooCommerce email it to the buyer instead, so use that one deliberately.

parameters.description: The order to attach the note to.

create_product.description: Add a product to the catalogue: name, description, SKU, regular and sale price with an optional sale window, categories, images, stock tracking, weight, tax status and visibility. Published straight away unless you choose a different status.
create_product.name: create_product

parameters.description: The product's name, as shoppers see it.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: What kind of product this is. 'Simple' is a single item with one price. 'Variable' and 'Grouped' need variations or child products set up in wp-admin before they can be bought.
parameters.name: product_type

parameters.description: Whether the product is live in the shop. New products are published unless you choose otherwise.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: The full product description. HTML is allowed.
parameters.name: description

parameters.description: The summary shown beside the price. HTML is allowed.
parameters.name: short_description

parameters.description: Your own stock-keeping code. WooCommerce refuses a duplicate, so it has to be unique across the store.
parameters.name: sku

parameters.description: The normal price, as a plain number in the store's own currency - 19.99, not $19.99.
parameters.name: regular_price

parameters.description: The discounted price. Takes effect immediately unless a sale window is set below.
parameters.name: sale_price

parameters.description: When the sale price begins. Leave blank to start now.
parameters.name: sale_starts_at

parameters.description: When the sale price stops. Leave blank to keep it until the sale price is removed.
parameters.name: sale_ends_at

parameters.description: Which categories to file the product under. Pick from the store's categories, or type a category ID.
parameters.name: category_ids

parameters.description: Publicly reachable image URLs. WooCommerce downloads each one into the store's media library; the first becomes the main product image.
parameters.name: image_urls

parameters.description: Mark the product as featured.
parameters.name: featured

parameters.description: Where in the store the product can be found.
parameters.name: catalog_visibility

parameters.description: Turn on for something that is not shipped, such as a service or a booking.
parameters.name: virtual

parameters.description: Let WooCommerce count this product's stock. The stock quantity and backorder settings below only apply when this is on.
parameters.name: manage_stock

parameters.description: How many are in stock. Needs stock tracking to be on.
parameters.name: stock_quantity

parameters.description: Whether the product can be bought. Set directly when stock is not tracked; WooCommerce works it out from the quantity when it is.
parameters.name: stock_status

parameters.description: Whether the product can be bought once stock runs out. Needs stock tracking to be on.
parameters.name: backorders

parameters.description: The product's weight, as a plain number in the store's own weight unit.
parameters.name: weight

parameters.description: What part of this product's price is taxed.
parameters.name: tax_status

parameters.description: A custom sort position in the shop. Lower comes first.
parameters.name: menu_order

delete_coupon.description: Move a coupon to the WordPress trash, where it stops working but can still be restored - or erase it for good by turning on 'Delete permanently'. Returns the coupon as it was.

mock_response.description: 10% off everything for the autumn sale.

delete_coupon.name: delete_coupon

parameters.description: The coupon's numeric ID. 'List coupons' returns it as 'id'.
parameters.name: coupon_id

parameters.description: Leave off to move the coupon to the WordPress trash, where it can be restored. Turn on to erase it for good.
parameters.name: permanently

delete_customer.description: Delete a customer account for good. There is no trash for this one: a customer is a WordPress user, and WordPress does not trash users. Their past orders survive and simply become guest orders, since an order keeps its own billing details.
delete_customer.name: delete_customer

parameters.description: The customer's numeric ID.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: Hand any posts this user wrote to another user ID. Their orders are unaffected either way.
parameters.name: reassign_to

delete_order.description: Move an order to the WordPress trash, where it can still be restored - or erase it for good by turning on 'Delete permanently', which also takes it out of the store's sales figures. Returns the order as it was.
delete_order.name: delete_order

parameters.description: The order's numeric ID.
parameters.name: order_id

parameters.description: Leave off to move the order to the WordPress trash, where it can be restored. Turn on to erase it for good.
parameters.name: permanently

delete_product.description: Move a product to the WordPress trash, where it stops being sold but can still be restored - or erase it for good by turning on 'Delete permanently'. Returns the product as it was.
delete_product.name: delete_product

parameters.description: The product's numeric ID. 'List products' returns it as 'id', and it is the 'post' number in the wp-admin URL when you edit a product.
parameters.name: product_id

parameters.description: Leave off to move the product to the WordPress trash, where it can be restored. Turn on to erase it for good.
parameters.name: permanently
